query_ground_truth.workflow_task: As an engineering manager transitioning our sprint tracking infrastructure, I need to verify a complex Jira expression for our new automation rules before setting up our workspaces. Simultaneously, I need to check my authenticated identity in Linear to ensure the correct bot account is authorized, and clean up our project feed by archiving an obsolete status update that is no longer relevant to the team.
query_ground_truth.query: Archive an obsolete project update in Linear to clean up the workspace status feed.
query_ground_truth.rationale: Requires the Linear project update archiving tool to clean up old status updates.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if project_id unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Locate/disambiguate the target project using LINEAR_LIST_LINEAR_PROJECTS (filter by name/metadata) and confirm the chosen project_id before any write.
[Optional (for verification before write)] [Prerequisite]: Fetch current status/state using LINEAR_GET_LINEAR_PROJECT (ensure you’re updating the intended project).

[Optional (if status_id/state mapping unclear)] [Prerequisite]: Derive the correct target status/state using LINEAR_RUN_QUERY_OR_MUTATION (query valid project statuses/fields) to avoid invalid updates.
[Required] [Step]: Update the project using LINEAR_UPDATE_LINEAR_PROJECT (set project_id plus supported statusId/state, e.g., planned/completed).
[Optional (if LINEAR_UPDATE_LINEAR_PROJECT errors or field unsupported)] [Fallback]: Apply the change via LINEAR_RUN_QUERY_OR_MUTATION (projectUpdate mutation) and confirm returned project fields.
[Optional (for verification after write)] [Next Step]: Confirm final status via LINEAR_GET_LINEAR_PROJECT (re-check state/status fields).
known_pitfalls: [LINEAR_UPDATE_LINEAR_PROJECT] Wrong/guessed statusId/state can fail with INPUT_ERROR (e.g., “status not found” at GraphQL path projectUpdate); derive valid targets first.
[LINEAR_RUN_QUERY_OR_MUTATION] status_code=400 GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED if enums/strings are typed incorrectly; pass values via variables with correct GraphQL types.
[LINEAR_RUN_QUERY_OR_MUTATION] Some setups return “Invalid request data provided.” unless headers include Content-Type: application/json and apollo-require-preflight: true (CSRF-like 400).
[LINEAR_RUN_QUERY_OR_MUTATION] Response payloads may be nested under response.data.data (not response.data.*), which can break naive parsers.
[LINEAR_LIST_LINEAR_PROJECTS] Name-based matches can be ambiguous and may require pagination/extra filtering to avoid selecting the wrong project_id.

LINEAR_UPDATE_LINEAR_PROJECT.description: Tool to update an existing Linear project. Use when you need to modify project properties like name, description, state, dates, or lead. All fields except project_id are optional - only provide the fields you want to update.

color.description: Color for the project (hex color code).

state.description: The state of the project. Standard values: 'backlog', 'planned', 'started', 'completed', 'canceled'. Note: Some workspaces may have custom states configured.

lead_id.description: The UUID of the user who will lead this project. Must be a valid Linear user UUID. Use the LIST_LINEAR_USERS action to get valid user IDs.

priority.description: Priority level of the project. 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Normal, 4 = Low.

status_id.description: The UUID of the project status to set. Must be a valid Linear project status UUID.

project_id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the project to update. This is the internal Linear ID, not the project slug or name.

start_date.description: New planned start date. Accepts various formats including YYYY-MM-DD, ISO datetime strings (e.g., 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z), or Unix timestamps. Will be normalized to YYYY-MM-DD format for the API.

examples: Updated project scope and objectives for Q1.
Redesigned onboarding flow with new user feedback.
description.description: New description for the project. Supports plain text.

target_date.description: New planned completion date. Accepts various formats including YYYY-MM-DD, ISO datetime strings (e.g., 2024-06-30T23:59:59Z), or Unix timestamps. Will be normalized to YYYY-MM-DD format for the API.

LINEAR_GET_LINEAR_PROJECT.description: Retrieves a single Linear project by its unique identifier. Use when verifying a newly created or updated project, or when fetching detailed project information by ID.

project_id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the Linear project to retrieve.

include_teams.description: Whether to include teams associated with the project in the response.

include_members.description: Whether to include project members in the response.

include_initiatives.description: Whether to include related initiatives in the response.

LINEAR_LIST_LINEAR_PROJECTS.description: Retrieves all projects from the Linear account. Returns a flat array (not a GraphQL connection) with fields id and name; use LINEAR_RUN_QUERY_OR_MUTATION for progress, state, issues, or team linkage. No server-side filtering: all workspace projects are returned regardless of team or name — filter client-side. Multiple projects can share identical names; always confirm project_id before downstream use. Results are permission-scoped to the connected user. Pagination: loop while page_info.hasNextPage is true, passing page_info.endCursor as after, or results will be silently truncated. HTTP 429 may occur in large workspaces; apply exponential backoff between calls.

after.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the `endCursor` from the previous response's `page_info` to fetch the next page.

first.description: Number of projects to return per page. Use with `after` to paginate through all projects.
